quickAnswer: Grafton has one of the larger renter populations in MetroWest (27.3% of households, 10th of 50 towns) and almost no bottled gas (1.5%, 47th of 50). Heat comes mostly from utility gas and oil, in homes with a median build year of 1978.
body: ## Three villages, mill-era streets and a lot of tenants

Grafton is really three places that share a name: North Grafton, Grafton and South Grafton, each with its own ZIP Code. The town also includes old Blackstone River mill villages such as Farnumsville and Fisherville. According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 2,067 of Grafton's 7,573 occupied households rent, which is 27.3% and the 10th-highest share among the 50 towns we serve. The middle town sits at 16.4%.
That matters because in a rented home the landlord usually picks the heating equipment, and the tenants live with the choice.
## What the mill history left behind

North Grafton's Upper Mill, now the Washington Mills complex, was built in 1826 as the New England Manufacturing Company, and mill housing went up at 12, 14 and 16 Overlook Street. Those central-chimney homes were boarding houses whose decorative trim has since been lost. Grafton also belongs to the Blackstone River Valley National Heritage Corridor, described as the oldest industrialized region in the U.S.

Central-chimney houses are a good example of why we do not quote from a catalog. A single big central chimney can limit where a boiler flue goes and how heat has to travel. Houses like that may need a creative route for pipes or a few ductless heads instead of a full duct system.
## Gas and oil, with LP almost missing

Utility gas heats 3,832 homes (50.6%) and fuel oil or kerosene heats 2,399 (31.7%). Electricity heats 1,094 (14.4%), which ranks 14th of 50 and sits above the 10.1% median of the group. Bottled or tank gas heats only 111 homes (1.5%), 47th of 50. Wood heats 90 homes.

In plain terms, a Grafton homeowner whose boiler dies is usually choosing between staying with gas, staying with oil, or moving to a heat pump. There is rarely a propane tank to swap out. Oil customers may have the most to gain from a heat pump, since oil means deliveries and an annual tune-up.
## An even spread of ages

The housing is balanced across the decades. 1,191 homes (15.2%) date from 1939 or earlier, 1,218 (15.6%) from 1940 to 1959, 1,706 (21.8%) from 1960 to 1979, 1,985 (25.4%) from 1980 to 1999, and 1,726 (22.1%) from 2000 on. The median home was built in 1978, a little newer than the 1975 median of the middle town, and the median owner-occupied value is $453,000, which ranks 39th. Older houses tend to leak more air, so their heating load can be much larger than a newer house of the same size. We assess the heating load before we quote.
## The electric utility and the rebates

National Grid is the confirmed electric utility for Grafton, so Mass Save is the first rebate program to look at for a 2026 heat pump. The whole-home rebate tops out at $8,500, and the weatherization and installer conditions come with it. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com. The [heat pump page](/cities/grafton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the details.
## Where we work in town

Whether the call comes from North Grafton, Grafton or South Grafton, the order is the same: we look at the building, size the equipment from the house, and hand over a free written estimate before work starts. Mass HVAC is based in Milford, and the Grafton and Upton Railroad, which runs freight between North Grafton and Milford, links the two towns.

faq.q: Is a heat pump realistic for a Grafton house that now burns oil?
faq.a: Often yes. Oil heats 31.7% of occupied Grafton homes, and those households buy fuel by delivery. A cold-climate heat pump can replace or reduce that, and the 2026 Mass Save rebate may apply if the home passes the weatherization test. We calculate the heating load first, then say whether a full or partial setup fits.

faq.q: Who is responsible for heat in a Grafton rental?
faq.a: The landlord, unless the lease says otherwise. The state sanitary code (105 CMR 410.201) sets a daytime floor of 68 F and a night floor of 64 F during the heating season, roughly mid-September to mid-June. With 2,067 Grafton households renting (27.3%), tenants and owners of rental buildings meet this rule often. It is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: Do old mill-era houses in Grafton need a different kind of heating system?
faq.a: They can. Houses from the nineteenth century often have small rooms, odd chimney locations and little duct space. A new boiler on existing radiators may fit best, or ductless heads may suit rooms that never had ducts. We look at the building before recommending anything.

faq.q: How does Grafton's home value compare with the rest of MetroWest?
faq.a: The median owner-occupied home is worth $453,000 (ACS 2022), which ranks 39th of 50 towns. The middle town sits at $579,150. Grafton also ranks 38th for detached share and 17th for multi-unit buildings, so the housing stock is more varied than a typical suburb. We size equipment from the individual house, not from town averages.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: In Grafton, 3,832 occupied homes heat with utility gas and 2,399 with oil, while bottled gas is nearly absent. A failed boiler is usually a choice between gas, oil or a heat pump, and we size it from your house.
body: ## A replacement decision with only three real options

Only 111 Grafton homes use bottled or tank gas, so the replacement question is usually gas, oil or a heat pump. If your system runs on gas, a new high-efficiency boiler or furnace is the like-for-like answer. If it runs on oil, you can stay with oil, convert to gas if a main passes your house, or step to a heat pump. Homes heated with electricity can also gain from a heat pump.
### Old construction, new boiler

Older houses with radiators or baseboard on hot-water loops can often keep those pipes when the boiler is replaced, which is usually the least disruptive route. What changes is the boiler size, since an old oversized unit was often matched to a leakier house than the one you have after new windows or insulation.
### What goes into a heating load assessment

- Floor area and ceiling height, room by room.
- Window type and condition, and the attic and wall insulation you can see.
- How much air leaks in around doors, sills and chimneys.
- The number of zones and the pipe or duct layout you already have.
A boiler picked from this list fits the house.
### Gas work needs a permit

A new gas appliance in Grafton does not go in on a handshake. The job needs a permit, a licensed plumber or gas fitter has to pull it, and an inspector signs off at the end. Venting and gas piping are planned with that final inspection in mind.
### Apartments and three-deckers

The 2022 ACS counts 451 homes in two-unit buildings, 473 in buildings of three or four units and 859 in buildings of five or more. When one boiler heats several households, a failure becomes a shared emergency. The [town overview](/cities/grafton) covers the minimum-temperature rules for rentals.
### Repair or replace

A single failed part on a younger unit is usually a repair. Age matters in Grafton in two ways: 1,985 homes date from 1980 to 1999 and 1,191 from 1939 or earlier, so we ask when the boiler went in, not only when the house was built. A cracked heat exchanger or repeat repairs point toward replacement.

faq.q: Should I convert my Grafton oil boiler to gas?
faq.a: Only if a gas main is available at your street and the connection makes sense for your situation. Oil heats 2,399 occupied Grafton homes and utility gas heats 3,832, so both paths are common here. Some households are better served by a new oil boiler, others by a heat pump. We compare these at the estimate, using your actual house.

faq.q: Can you replace a boiler without changing my radiators?
faq.a: In most hot-water systems, yes. The piping and radiators can usually stay, though they are checked for leaks and pressure as part of the job. In older Grafton houses with radiators, that keeps the work contained to the boiler room and the flue, which is often the least disruptive route.

faq.q: Who do I call when the heat fails at night?
faq.a: Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. We take emergency calls around the clock, and a free written estimate comes before any repair or replacement work begins. In a rental, tell your landlord as well, since the landlord normally pays for heat and the state sets minimum indoor temperatures during the heating season.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Grafton is 62.3% detached houses, 15.0% townhouse-style homes and 22.8% multi-unit buildings, with a median build year of 1978. Cooling that suits a duplex may not suit a detached house, so we match the system to the building.
body: ## Cooling a mixed town

In the Census Bureau's 2022 survey, Grafton counts 4,873 detached houses, 1,170 attached homes and 1,783 homes in multi-unit buildings. That mix produces very different cooling jobs under one town name.
### Detached houses

A detached house built after the 1980s often has ductwork designed with air conditioning in mind, and a condenser pad is simple to find. Older houses often lack that, but they can still be cooled with a high-velocity small-duct system or with ductless heads.
### Townhouses and condos
Attached homes share walls, so equipment may have to fit tight outdoor space and meet association rules. Quiet operation can matter more when neighbors are close.
### Apartment buildings

Grafton has 859 homes in buildings with 5 or more units and 473 in buildings with 3 or 4 units. In these, a ductless unit per apartment can be the practical option, because each household controls its own system and one failure does not leave the whole building warm.
### Questions we ask first

- Which rooms overheat, and at what time of day?
- Is there a basement or attic route for ducts, or not?
- Is the electrical panel ready for new equipment?
- Is a unit that also heats worth pricing next to a cooling-only one? The [heat pump page](/cities/grafton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains the trade-offs.
### Sizing for humidity

Grafton ranks 38th of 50 for single-family detached share and 17th for multi-unit buildings. The middle town is 76.7% detached and 16.1% multi-unit, so a cooling quote here covers a wider spread of building types than in a typical MetroWest suburb. There are also 451 homes in two-unit buildings, a size that sits between the house and the apartment block.
### When the air conditioner stops

A warm house is not always a dead unit. Weak cooling can come from a small repairable fault, and the estimate separates repairs from replacement. A compressor failure on an old unit is the case most likely to tip toward a new system.

faq.q: Can a house with radiators get central air?
faq.a: Sometimes, but it depends on whether ducts can be fitted. Where they cannot, ductless mini-splits or a small-duct system cool the house without major construction. Grafton has 1,191 homes from 1939 or earlier and 1,218 from 1940 to 1959, and many older homes were built without central air, so this question comes up regularly.

faq.q: What size air conditioner does my house need?
faq.a: It depends on the load, not the square footage alone. Insulation, windows and sun exposure all count. We measure those factors rather than copy the size of the old unit. A unit that is too large cools quickly, then shuts off before it has pulled moisture out of the air.

faq.q: Does Grafton's mix of homes change what cooling I should ask about?
faq.a: Yes. The town has 4,873 detached houses, 1,170 attached homes (15.0%) and 1,783 homes in multi-unit buildings (22.8%). A detached house needs ductwork or ductless heads and a spot for the outdoor unit. An attached home may have less outdoor room. An apartment usually suits one ductless unit per household.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Grafton is on National Grid's territory list, so Mass Save's 2026 whole-home heat pump rebate of $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, is the first program to check. The home must pass a weatherization test.
body: ## Rebates for Grafton customers of National Grid

National Grid serves Grafton, so Mass Save is the program to check first. The 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and the home must be weatherized first. The full conditions are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Grafton's ages against the 2000 line

Only 1,726 Grafton homes (22.1%) date from 2000 or later. The other bands were built earlier: 1,191 from 1939 or before, 1,218 from 1940 to 1959, 1,706 from 1960 to 1979 and 1,985 from 1980 to 1999. For most of them, an energy assessment is the practical first step before a whole-home heat pump goes in.
### Who should look hardest

Oil is the fuel to watch here, even though Grafton ranks 29th of 50 for oil, below the 36.5% median. The 2,399 oil homes pay for deliveries and an annual cleaning, and a heat pump removes some or all of that. The 1,094 electric-heat homes may use less electricity for the same warmth. Gas homes are a closer call, because gas is often cheaper per unit of heat, so the case is less clear and depends on the house.
### Whole-home or partial
### Electricity, LP and the rest

Electric heat is above the middle: 14.4% of occupied homes, 14th of 50, against a 10.1% median. At the other end, bottled gas heats 111 homes and ranks 47th, wood heats 90 and 47 homes use other fuel or coal. Those 1,094 electric-heat homes are the ones where a heat pump swaps one electric heat source for another.
A whole-home setup aims to carry the heating load alone. A partial setup leaves the existing boiler for the coldest days, and its rebate is calculated differently.
### Ductless in village houses and apartments

Older houses often lack usable ducts. A ductless mini-split puts a small indoor head in each space, with one outdoor unit and a thin line set through the wall. The same approach suits additions, finished attics and apartments in the town's multi-unit buildings, as the [cooling page](/cities/grafton/air-conditioning-installation-repair) describes.
### Sizing is the real skill
A heat pump that is too small runs flat out and struggles in a cold week. One that is too big cycles on and off. We calculate the home's heating load before we quote.

faq.q: Is my Grafton home eligible for the whole-home rebate?
faq.a: Probably, if the work is done in 2026, the installer is eligible and the home passes the weatherization test. National Grid is the confirmed utility for Grafton. An assessment settles the weatherization point for most houses. Terms change, so confirm them at masssave.com and on our main heat pump page.

faq.q: Will a heat pump replace my oil boiler completely?
faq.a: It can when the system is sized for the full heating load, which is why we assess the load before quoting. Another route keeps the boiler for the coldest days, and we discuss both options before you commit. With 2,399 oil-heated homes in Grafton, this is one of the more common questions we expect.

faq.q: Does a ductless system need ducts?
faq.a: No. Each indoor head connects to the outdoor unit through a small hole in the wall. That suits rooms and buildings with no ducts, such as finished attics, additions and apartments in the 1,783 homes in Grafton's multi-unit buildings. Each head can be placed in the room that needs it.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With 2,399 oil-heated homes and 3,832 on gas in Grafton, a yearly tune-up before heating season is the usual rule. Servicing early is also worth it for rental buildings, where one failure can leave several households cold.
body: ## Tune-ups by fuel

In Grafton the service call depends on what is in your cellar. An oil system gets its yearly cleaning: burner, nozzle, filter and a combustion test. Gas systems need a check of burners, venting, controls and heat exchanger. A heat pump visit centers on coils, filters and the refrigerant side. Wood users should have flues inspected before they light the first fire.
### Landlords and tenants

Grafton ranks 10th of 50 for renter share (27.3%, against a 16.4% median), so a tune-up on a multi-unit boiler can protect more than one family. A boiler that fails on a January night is an urgent call and often an avoidable one. A check in early fall catches weak ignition, leaks and worn circulators.
### What a visit includes

- Cleaning and inspecting the main components.
- Checking safety controls and flue draft.
- Testing thermostat operation.
- Noting anything likely to fail soon so you can plan the cost.
### The calendar

- **September and October:** heating checks before the first frost.
- **April and May:** air conditioner and mini-split checks.
- **Any time:** call early for short cycling, odd smells or an unusual noise.
### What owners can do
Oil customers on delivery can watch the tank level between visits, since 2,399 Grafton homes burn oil or kerosene.
### Age matters

Grafton's median home was built in 1978. In houses of that age, older burners and pumps wear out in predictable ways, and a tune-up is the cheapest time to spot them. Newer equipment, such as in the 450 homes built since 2010, still needs yearly checks of its safety controls and venting, and gas is the fuel for 50.6% of the town's occupied homes. For heating replacement guidance, see the [heating page](/cities/grafton/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: When should I schedule an oil burner cleaning?
faq.a: Ideally late summer or early fall, before the system runs daily. Once a year is the usual rule for oil, because soot builds up and can reduce efficiency or cause a shutdown. Grafton has 2,399 oil or kerosene homes.

faq.q: Does a newer gas furnace still need servicing?
faq.a: Usually yes. Newer equipment still collects dust and needs its safety controls and venting checked. Grafton has 450 homes built in 2010 or later, only 5.8% of the housing stock and 37th of 50 towns, and gas heats 50.6% of occupied homes. Yearly checks keep small faults from turning into winter calls.

faq.q: Who should book the boiler check in a rental building?
faq.a: Usually the landlord, who normally pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise, and who often owns the boiler too. With 2,067 renter households in Grafton, 451 homes in two-unit buildings and 859 in buildings of five or more, one boiler often serves several households. An early fall check is far easier to arrange than a January failure, and the town's 27.3% renter share, 10th of 50, makes the question a common one.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Grafton homes run from mill-era houses (15.2% date from 1939 or earlier) to newer builds (5.8% since 2010). The air problem depends on which kind of house you have, so we start with the house.
body: ## Air in a town of every age

Grafton's housing is spread evenly over the decades, so no single air problem describes it. The 2022 ACS counts 1,191 units from 1939 or earlier, 1,218 from 1940 to 1959, 1,706 from 1960 to 1979, 1,985 from 1980 to 1999 and 1,726 from 2000 on, with 450 of those since 2010.
### Old houses

Houses from the mill era tend to leak air around sills, chimneys and windows. That brings in dust, pollen and damp basement air, and it makes humidity swing from season to season. Before renovating a house of that age, have a qualified specialist test for older materials.
### Newer, tighter houses

A newer house holds air in. That can save energy, but moisture and cooking fumes stay inside unless ventilation is working. Grafton has 1,726 homes built since 2000, and 450 of those date from 2010 on, so tight construction is a real part of the stock.
### Humidity and the basement

Winter air is dry once the heat is on, and summer brings dampness. Cellars in older houses can hold moisture all year. A dehumidifier manages the air, while a leak or drainage fault needs its own fix.
### Filters and ducts

- A better filter catches more, but the system must be able to pull air through it.
- Duct cleaning is a judgment call made after an inspection.
- Whole-home humidifiers and dehumidifiers can be tied to the system.
- Ventilation can be added to a tight house.
### Apartments

With 859 homes in buildings of five or more units, 473 in three- or four-unit buildings and 451 in two-unit houses, air can pass between neighbors through shared walls and chases. That is often a building-wide job. Our [maintenance page](/cities/grafton/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) explains how filters and coils fit in.

faq.q: Should I have my Grafton ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. We inspect first and tell you whether cleaning is worthwhile. Cleaning is a fair request after a renovation or a pest problem, and less so for ducts in good condition. In a town with 1,985 homes built from 1980 to 1999, ducts are often a mid-life system, so condition matters more than age.

faq.q: Why does my house feel dry in winter?
faq.a: Cold outdoor air holds little moisture, and heating it makes indoor air drier. A humidifier tied to the system can raise comfort, but keep humidity moderate so windows do not fog or grow mold. Older homes that leak more air often swing more, while a tight house holds whatever humidity is made inside.

faq.q: Do Grafton's older houses and newer ones need different air fixes?
faq.a: Often, yes. Houses from 1939 or earlier (1,191 in town) tend to leak, so sealing and moisture control matter. The 1,726 homes built since 2000 tend to be tighter, so ventilation matters more. The 1960 to 1999 houses sit between, and we look at each one before suggesting anything.
